title: "upgrade-loop refinements: converged-skip healing, rc 0 with skips, no direction guard"
body:
# 0021: upgrade-loop refinements: converged-skip healing, rc 0 with skips, no direction guard

## Tags

upgrade, manifest, exit-status, direction, audit

## Summary

Three findings from the 2026-08-24 upgrade audit, one file, one verb, none blocking (the fleet sweep ran green under all three). Bundled because a fix pass over `lib/cmd/upgrade` would take them together.

1. **Converged-skip stickiness.** The modified-vs-manifest check precedes the source-equality compare (lib/cmd/upgrade:128 vs :143), so a vendored file whose bytes now EQUAL the new canonical -- what a carried-then-upstreamed patch produces -- still skips as "edited in place", keeps its install-time checksum, and doctor stays red forever without `--force`. Measured: file == HEAD source, upgrade says skipped, doctor rc 1; `--force` is byte-safe exactly there (equality short-circuits, 0 updated, manifest heals).
2. **rc 0 with skips.** An upgrade that refused files still exits 0; the refusal is visible only in the report text. Measured. A scripted caller reading rc cannot distinguish clean from partial; the honest read is doctor-after or parsing the summary line.
3. **No direction guard.** Upgrade syncs from source unconditionally: a DOWNGRADE prints "updated" per file and doctor stays green. Measured -- 11 files silently reverted from an older `--from`. The manifest's `source_commit` (b433988) is the hook a warn-on-downgrade would need; nothing reads it today.

## Reproduction

All three in the 2026-08-24 audit session, scratch installs via the real installer (D24), fingerprint instrument negative-controlled before use.

## Root Cause

(1) is check ordering; (2) is a policy default ("own job completed; refusals reported"); (3) is a scope decision never taken -- the audit found no ruling either way.

## Impact

Sized against hv's 2026-08-24 Intentv3 ruling: (1)'s dominant producer -- Intent's transitional script vendoring -- dissolves at v3, so no durable machinery for Intent specifically; the fix stays worth having because the carry doctrine ("resolve upstream, do not fork") produces the shape at ANY consumer. (2) and (3) are latent until someone scripts a sweep or points `--from` at the wrong checkout; the 2026-08-24 sweep hit neither because it read output, not rc, and pulled from one verified source.

## Proposed Fix

(1) Compare `sum_src`/`sum_dst` BEFORE the modified-skip; on equality, treat as unchanged and record the checksum -- convergence is not divergence. (2) Either a distinct exit code for completed-with-skips, or an explicit ruling that rc stays 0 and the seal/report is the record -- decided, not defaulted. (3) Optional: warn when the target manifest's `source_commit` is not an ancestor of the source's HEAD; needs git in the loop, so it may be a `devbin vendor` (0017) concern rather than upgrade's.

## Related

- 0017 -- the vendor builtin, whose preview role overlaps (2) and whose vs-source comparison subsumes (3)
- 0014 -- the version-number axis vs git identity; (3) is that gap surfacing inside upgrade
- 0016 -- the carry doctrine that produces (1)'s shape

## Resolutions

**CLOSED 2026-08-24 (vc).** All three, in one pass over `lib/cmd/upgrade` with 0017's `vendor` -- which is what made (2) and (3) answerable rather than merely fixable.

**(1) Converged-skip stickiness -- FIXED, and red-checked on the defect itself.** The source-equality compare now runs BEFORE the modified-vs-manifest refusal, and an equal file is recorded from disk rather than added to `preserved`, which is the heal. Upgrade prints `converged  <path> (your edit is now upstream -- tracking it again)`.

The red-check is the part worth keeping. With the old ordering restored, the test fails on exactly the right line: upgrade prints `skipped bin/.devbin/lib/helpers` for a file whose bytes already match the source, and then tells the reader those files "differ from what was installed" -- which is TRUE of the manifest and FALSE of the source. That sentence is the defect in one line: two baselines, one word. Reordering cannot cost a file, because nothing is written on either branch; they differ only in what the manifest ends up recording.

**(2) rc 0 with skips -- RULED, not defaulted, which is what the issue asked for.** Upgrade's exit status stays 0 when files were refused. Its status answers "did I complete", and a run that reported every refusal and wrote a correct manifest DID complete. The other question -- is this tree level with its source -- now has its own command whose status means only that, so neither has to be read out of the other's exit code. A scripted sweep asserts convergence with `vendor`, and upgrade points at it in the skip summary. Recorded in `usage-rules.md` as a NEVER, since the failure mode is a caller reading 0 as convergence. **hv can reverse this in one line if a distinct completed-with-skips code is wanted instead.**

**(3) Direction guard -- IMPLEMENTED as a warning.** `source_direction` in `lib/install` compares the recorded `source_commit` to the source's HEAD and answers `same` / `forward` / `backward` / `unrelated` / `unknown`. Upgrade warns before writing on `backward` and `unrelated`, naming both commits and pointing at `vendor`. It warns rather than refuses: pinning a consumer while a regression is investigated is a real thing to do, and a tool that refused it would only be run with a flag nobody reads. What was missing was never permission; it was being told.

**`unknown` is a real answer and never reads as `forward`.** Four ordinary causes: a manifest predating the `source_commit` field, a source that was not a checkout, recorded bytes that were dirty and match no commit, and a clone that simply does not have the commit. The last needs `cat-file -e` before the ancestry test, because `merge-base --is-ancestor` returns 1 both for "not an ancestor" and for a commit it has never heard of -- which are `unrelated` and `unknown`, and collapsing them would be the same wrong-baseline error one level down.

**Found while building, and fixed here:** the report header printed the source's bare `HEAD` while the comparison read its WORKING TREE, so a dirty source would have shown a clean-looking sha beside a `level` verdict -- a confident false statement of exactly the kind the `source_commit` field was added to stop. It now prints `source_commit_of`, which says `+dirty -- THESE BYTES MATCH NO COMMIT` when that is the truth. Red-checked. `_source_commit` was promoted to `source_commit_of` at the same time: an underscore on a function a second file depends on is a false signal about its contract.
